chunks: From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Dorust al-Wasiti, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abdul Rahman al-Qasir, who said:

I said to him, 'Does the believer visit his family?' He said, 'Yes. He seeks permission from his Lord, so He grants it. He sends two angels with him, and they come to them in one of the forms of birds, alighting in his house, looking at them, and hearing their speech.'
ai.seo_question: How does a deceased believer visit their family according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, this narration highlights the Shia belief in the continued spiritual presence of the deceased, who seeks divine permission to visit their family accompanied by two angels. The imagery of appearing in the form of birds (*surat al-tayr*) suggests a subtle, non-physical manifestation that allows the soul to observe and listen to the living without being fully perceived, emphasizing the enduring bond between the departed and the bereaved.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Dorost Al Wasity, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Abdul Rahman who said,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The Believer visits his family?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. He seeks Permission of his Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, so it is Permitted for him. So He<sup>azwj</sup> Sends two Angels along with him, and they come over to them in one of the images of the birds, falling upon his wall, looking at them, and hears their speech’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from him (narrator of above Hadith) from Isma’il ibn Mehran from Durust ibn abu Mansur al-Wasitiy from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from ‘Abd al- Rahim al-Qasir who has said the following:

“I asked the Imam, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Does a deceased believing person visit his family?’ He replied, ‘Yes, he asks his Lord for permission; then by His permission with two angels he comes to his family in the form of some kind of a bird. He turns arround his house and observes his family and hears whatever they say.’”
